sentences.text: Sinocalliopteryx was a carnivorous theropod dinosaur that walked on two legs.
Its skull measured up to 29 centimetres in length and held numerous serrated, conical teeth in the premaxillae alongside curved teeth in the maxillae.
Protofeathers covered the back of the skull, neck, back, hips, tail, and parts of the limbs, with the longest feathers located on the hips, the base of the tail, and the rear portions of the femur.
The original 2007 specimen was the largest known member of the Compsognathidae family, measuring 2.37 meters in length and estimated to weigh twenty kilograms.
The holotype skeleton contained a preserved dromaeosaurid leg inside its abdominal cavity, including a tibia fragment measuring 15.5 cm in length.
Remains of at least two Confuciusornis sanctus birds and a 13.5-centimetre scapula from a 1.5-metre-long herbivorous ornithischian were found in the second specimen.
The species Sinocalliopteryx gigas was first named and described in 2007 by a team of four researchers who excavated the holotype in Hengdaozi, Sihetun locality, Beipiao, west Liaoning province.

The original fossil specimen was found at Hengdaozi in Liaoning Province, China, and dates to about 125 million years ago, while there are two recorded fossil occurrences of Sinocalliopteryx in the Paleobiology Database.

Researchers suggested the preserved prey leg indicates Sinocalliopteryx preyed on smaller, bird-like dinosaurs, and the capture of multiple birds suggests it may have specialized in bird prey as a ground-dwelling predator using stealth attacks.
The stones in the abdomen were interpreted as gastroliths similar to those found in other theropods, though no special gizzard would have been present in Sinocalliopteryx.
The original researchers assigned Sinocalliopteryx to the family Compsognathidae, and it is classified within this group as the parent group of the species.
Sinocalliopteryx is considered the last member of the family Compsognathidae to be discovered.

Sinocalliopteryx was a carnivorous theropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Lower Cretaceous period, approximately 124.6 million years ago, specifically during the Barremian to Aptian stages from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
Fossils were found in Liaoning province, northeast China, where the flora included conifers such as pines and araucarias.

A 2024 study by Andrea Cau questioned the classification of Sinocalliopteryx within the Compsognathidae family, with recent analyses suggesting it may belong to a group called Sinosauropterygidae instead.

Recent analyses suggest Sinocalliopteryx is phylogenetically closer to Guanlong, Proceratosaurus, and Mirischia than originally thought, leading to debates on whether it and related genera should be placed within Tyrannosauroidea despite being closer to birds than tyrannosauroids.
